args.text:
MAMMOTH HOT SPRINGS, Wyo. – Good news for fishos: from Friday, Sept. 4, the last of the fishin' restrictions on the Firehole, Madison and Gibbon (downstream of Norris Campground) rivers, and every creek that runs into 'em, are comin' off, now the weather and the water have cooled down. Ya'll be able to fish these rivers, along with most of the park's other rivers, creeks and lakes, every day from sunup to sundown, like it says in the 2026 Fishing Regulations booklet.

These rivers were shut to fishin' altogether back on July 15, then that got wound back to part-day restrictions on Aug. 28 once things picked up. The restrictions and closures had to happen while the water was low and the water temperatures were over 68 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius), which can kill fish.

Staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures, mind. Depending on how things are lookin', they might bring in temporary restrictions or closures again.

Update: Yellowstone lifts full closures for Firehole, Madison and Gibbon rivers

Part-day restrictions still on from 2 p.m. to sunup the next day

MAMMOTH HOT SPRINGS, Wyo. – From Friday, Aug. 28, fishos can have a go at the Firehole, Madison and Gibbon (downstream of Norris Campground) rivers, and every creek that runs into 'em, from sunup till 2 p.m. each day. With the weather and the water coolin' off, and a bit of rain in the forecast too, the full closures can come off.

The full closures went on back on July 15, cos low water and water temperatures over 68 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius) can kill fish. The water's been coolin' off overnight, so there's fishin' for part of the day now. Ya can still fish most of the park's other rivers, creeks and lakes every day from sunup to sundown, like it says in the 2026 Fishing Regulations booklet.

Staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures. Depending on how things are lookin', the temporary restrictions might come off, or there might be more closures.

Fishos: Do us a favour and fish in the coolest part of the day, and land yer fish quick. Don't play a hooked trout till it's knackered. Handle fish gently, in the water as much as ya can, and give 'em a chance to come good before ya let 'em go. If everyone does the right thing, it'll look after the park's fisheries, and it might save 'em havin' to ban fishin' at all hours on some rivers and creeks if things get worse.
